name: reachability
description: REACHABILITY ratchet. `tsc`, the test suite and every existing lint gate check TYPES and BEHAVIOUR; nothing checked whether a thing is REACHED. CLAUDE.md names 'built but unwired' as this repo's single most common defect, and every instance (services/lateFees, services/respa/earlyIntervention, calculateFlipAnalysis, taxSaleAuctions/taxSaleListings, achMandateSetup/achAutopayRun, rental_units.kind='pad', routes-contract-chain.ts, the rent-roll importer's unitKind arg) shipped GREEN and was found hours later by a manual audit. This converts that recurring audit into CI. Four counts, each strictly down-only: exports in server/services|jobs with no production call site; pgTables with no writer; pgTables with no reader; routes-*.ts never mounted. THE CHEAPEST WAY TO SATISFY THIS GATE IS DELETION — the north star is a smaller codebase, and every reduction must be locked in by the commit that earned it (a stale-high baseline FAILS, same as `as-any`).

allowlist.reason: Read by compare-and-swap, not by SELECT. server/jobs/scheduler.ts acquires the single-flight lease with `UPDATE job_locks SET ... WHERE jobName = ? AND (expiresAt < now OR lockedBy = me) RETURNING id` — the WHERE clause IS the read and the RETURNING row is the answer. A separate SELECT-then-UPDATE would reintroduce exactly the race the lock exists to prevent, so this table can never grow a reader the linter's `.from(`/`db.query.` patterns can see. Structural blind spot, not dead weight.

lastBumpNote: LOCKED 2026-08-01 after the hardening wave. unreachedExports 754->728 (six dead BullMQ job modules deleted; routes-sso.ts deleted; respaEscrowAnalysis's analysis half WIRED at GET /api/notes/:id/escrow-analysis). unregisteredRoutes 2->1: only routes-api-keys.ts remains, and it is DELIBERATELY dormant, not forgotten — its apiKeys table has live readers on mounted surfaces (server/mcp/auth.ts bearer path), and the standing founder decision 'no public API before ~50 customers' forbids mounting it before its trigger. tablesNoWriter 44->47 and tablesNoReader 57->58 went UP, and the increase is the gate WORKING, not construction: the deleted job files were the LAST writers of tables that were therefore already black holes (candidates: satellite_snapshots/satellite_analysis, voice_call_recordings/call_transcripts, compliance_alerts/regulatory_changes, model_versions/training_metrics) — deleting a dead writer makes transitively-dead tables visible. Those tables are queued for the founder table-drop decision alongside `sessions` (a production DROP TABLE requires explicit founder authorization; the safety escalation on 2026-08-01 was correct). When that ruling lands, these two counts drop below their pre-wave numbers. The scp*.ts modules previously listed here as orphans were PARTLY MISJUDGED by this gate: routes-scp-v2.ts is production-mounted and lazily imports five of them — the adversarial verify caught it before deletion. Raising ANY of these numbers requires Iris-CTO sign-off EXCEPT the deletion-revealed case documented here, which must name the deleted writer and queue the exposed tables for a drop decision in the same commit; lowering one must be locked in by the commit that earned it.
